$comment: Baseline of QUEUED, human-owned design-token contrast issues. audit-checks classifies each color-contrast violation against these signatures: a match is tagged `queued` (already logged for a foundation decision — do NOT re-verify per component), anything else is a NEW finding that needs review. Match is by foreground hex (and background hex when given), case-insensitive.
$resolved: The tone-as-text and solid white-on-tone contrast family (destructive/success/warning/sev-* used as message ink, delta ink, badge soft/outline/solid text, and alert text) was RESOLVED at the foundation: theme-aware `--<tone>-ink` text tokens meeting WCAG AA 4.5:1 on card/app/tint in both themes, `text-on-tone` (dark ink) for solid badge fills, and removal of the AlertDescription opacity dim. See the audit token-fix commit. FOLLOW-UP (this audit): the original `--*-ink` calibration only covered the soft tint composited over the DEFAULT app/card surface; a soft badge on a NESTED panel surface (e.g. Badge inside CodeBlock in tool-call-block) composites its 14%-alpha tint over that darker/lighter surface, dropping success-ink (3.92 dark / 4.45 light) and destructive-ink (4.01 dark / 4.46 light) below AA. Recalibrated `--success-ink` and `--destructive-ink` in BOTH themes to clear 4.5:1 on the worst-case nested tint (>=4.6:1, hue preserved) — verified via axe. warning/sev-* inks are not exercised on a nested surface by any current consumer (no confirmed failure); if a future consumer places them on a nested panel, apply the same nested-tint recalibration. The previously-queued `contrast` signatures below are cleared; any remaining tone-contrast is now a NEW finding.
$exemptions: Disabled/inactive UI text (e.g. file-card/file-list with data-[disabled]:opacity-55) is WCAG 1.4.3-exempt and is not a token issue — audit agents should treat dimmed disabled-state text as exempt, not a NEW finding.
